test_add_line_comment_slice_delete_parse.rationale: Change A keeps the closing bracket off a trailing add_line comment so the output parses. Change B alters which rendered groups a slice deletion removes, and so changes what is left for A's branch to render. With B, del a[:-1] leaves a lone group that carries the comment ('[\n    2 # c]'), and a no-op del a[:0] keeps the comment group too. A must still produce parseable output in these post-deletion layouts. Without A the bracket is swallowed by the comment.

test_add_line_comment_slice_delete_sync..rationale: Change B makes slice deletion keep the rendered array consistent with the list contents. This checks that it does so for arrays built with add_line(comment=...), whose rendering Change A modifies. Under B, a negative-stop slice must drop the leading value while keeping the trailing comment, and a stop==0 slice must not wipe the rendered values. The assertions inspect only the rendered content, not parseability, so they hold on B with or without A.

test_array_slice_and_render_invariants.p.rationale: Neither change should alter arrays that have no trailing comment as the last rendered element. A plain single-line array must stay on one line after an ordinary positive slice deletion. A parsed multiline array whose comment sits before the closing newline must still round-trip after a slice deletion. Both hold on the base and must keep holding after the merge.
